# Gateway configuration reference (`config.yaml`)

`config.yaml` defines LiteGate's listeners, certificates, service discovery, observability, caching, authentication and MCP exposure.

> [!TIP]
> MCP's `get_gateway_config_schema` returns this file verbatim. The fields here must stay in step with `internal/config/types.go`.

---

## 0. Mode

```yaml
# performance: high-throughput mode (default). Metrics, access logs, tracing and the dashboard still work when enabled
# observability: records routing details for every request and always feeds the dashboard live stream
mode: "performance"
```

`performance` (the default) only skips per-request accounting that nothing consumes: enabling `metrics`, `dashboard`, `log.access_log` or `tracing` keeps that feature fully working, and the dashboard live request stream keeps flowing while the dashboard is on. Use `mode: observability` to always record routing details.

---

## 1. Listeners and entrypoints (multiple ports / network interfaces)

LiteGate supports Traefik-style multiple ingress listeners, so different sites or an internal management interface can bind to different ports or to a specific physical interface (`SO_BINDTODEVICE`).

```yaml
entrypoints:
  web:
    address: ":80"
  websecure:
    address: ":443"
    tls: true
  # internal:
  #   address: ":8080"
  #   interface_name: "eth0"         # Optional. Bind a Linux network device, following its DHCP address

# Legacy port configuration; when entrypoints is present, entrypoints wins
http:
  port: 80
  https_port: 443
  response_header_timeout: 60    # Optional. Default response-header timeout, in seconds
  # upstream_transport_shards: 1  # Optional. Connection pools per upstream endpoint, to cut pool-lock contention under high concurrency; default 1 = off
  # upstream_buffer_size: 32768   # Optional. Upstream HTTP/1 connection read/write buffer in bytes (4096..65536, default 32768); large bodies bypass it
  # upstream_client: fast         # Optional. Default fast: plaintext HTTP/1.1 upstreams use a synchronous pool (lower overhead) and TLS/mTLS/HTTP2/gRPC/WebSocket automatically use the standard client; standard uses Go's net/http Transport everywhere
  # listen_backlog: 65535        # Optional. Windows only: TCP accept queue length (1..65535, default 65535). Needs a `make windows` build; Go's default is about 200, so connection bursts get refused
  # drain_delay: 5               # drain wait in seconds; omitted = auto, 0 = off, N = fixed N seconds
  # drain_delay_ms: 250          # optional millisecond override, taking precedence over drain_delay
```

**Shutdown drain (`drain_delay`)**: on a stop signal, `/readyz` starts returning 503 and LiteGate actively deregisters from Consul / litemesh, then waits before closing its listeners so load balancers in front stop sending new requests.

- **Omitted (default, auto)**: waits only when something is actually watching — when registered with Consul / litemesh it deregisters first and waits 1 second; when `/readyz` was probed within the last 2 minutes (K8s readinessProbe, a cloud load balancer) it waits 5 seconds; a standalone instance nobody probes stops immediately.
- `drain_delay: 0` disables the wait; `drain_delay: N` always waits N seconds (e.g. when the load balancer only does TCP checks, which auto-detection cannot see).
- Press Ctrl-C again (or send a second SIGTERM) during the wait to skip it.
- Upgrading: configs generated by older versions contain `drain_delay: 5`, which counts as an explicit setting and keeps the 5-second wait; delete that line to use auto mode.

`interface_name` binds a specific Linux network device and follows its DHCP address. The legacy `http` block still works; when `entrypoints` is present, `entrypoints` wins.

### 1.1 Ingress plugins

Compiled ingress plugins handle HTTP requests on explicitly selected entrypoints
before site matching and path normalization. Bindings execute in array order;
unhandled requests continue to the next plugin and then the site router. No
plugins are enabled by default. Names must be unique and entrypoints explicit.
Missing plugins, unknown entrypoints and invalid plugin options reject configuration.

```yaml
# The standard binary includes forward_proxy; declare a websecure TLS entrypoint first.
ingress_plugins:
  - name: developer-egress
    type: forward_proxy
    entrypoints: [websecure]
    config:
      username: developer
      hosts: [proxy.example.com]
      password: '$2a$10$REPLACE_WITH_COMPLETE_BCRYPT_HASH'
      probe_resistance: true
      hide_ip: true
      hide_via: true
      allowed_destinations: [example.org, "*.example.org"]
      allowed_ports: [80, 443]
```

Global ingress security runs first. Handled requests do not enter site middleware
; the host records access logs, metrics and dashboard traffic under `ingress:<binding name>`. The plugin owns authentication and destination policies. Internally injected
Forward/Connect traffic skips this chain. Failed candidate initialization keeps
the active instances; successful reloads drain old instances for `http.shutdown_grace` (30 seconds when unset), then cancel their host context and close them with a deadline. Shutdown closes their owned connections immediately.
Generate the full bcrypt hash with `litegate -hash 'your-password'` and place it in
`password`; clients use the original password. Alternatively set `password_env`
to read the original password from an environment variable. Configure exactly one;
plaintext `password` is rejected. Optional `hosts` matches TLS SNI, not CONNECT's
destination Host; unmatched, non-TLS or missing-SNI requests fall through. Configure
a normal or catch-all Site for unauthenticated requests when probe resistance is enabled.
A shared website listener must configure `hosts` or enable `probe_resistance`, otherwise legitimate absolute-form requests may receive 407. Changing only the value of the environment variable named by `password_env` does not rebuild an unchanged binding; change binding configuration or restart to load it.
Successful bcrypt authentication caches the header SHA-256 digest for 5 minutes, renewing the TTL on cache hits with constant-time comparison; each instance admits at most two concurrent bcrypt checks, waiting for admission for at most 100ms subject to the request context. Wildcards do not grant access to local interface addresses, `64:ff9b::/96`, `240.0.0.0/4` or `198.18.0.0/15`; intentional access requires explicit IP/CIDR rules. Each resolved address has its own dial timeout. Interface addresses are cached for 30 seconds and refreshed on demand. A cloud public IP behind 1:1 NAT may not appear on the interfaces; add it to `denied_destinations` to block connections back to the gateway. Changing only `shutdown_grace` keeps the reused instance’s original grace period; change the binding or restart to adopt the new value. HTTP/2/3 end both directions when download ends; half-close is retained only for hijacked HTTP/1 connections.
`hide_ip` and `hide_via` default to true, removing existing client-IP and Via headers
from forwarded HTTP requests. Setting them to false appends the client IP to Forwarded
and LiteGate to Via respectively. CONNECT payloads are never rewritten.
The plugin supports HTTP/1.1 forwarding and HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 CONNECT through the public
`RegisterIngress` API; see `examples/plugins/ingress/forwardproxy/README.md`.

### 1.2 SNI / L4 routing on shared 443

`entrypoints.websecure.routes` inspects the TLS ClientHello before HTTPS
termination and dispatches connections to an L4 backend or a named Stream.
Unmatched hostnames continue to normal HTTPS sites. Explicit transport routes
currently require `websecure` with `tls: true`.

#### Direct passthrough to a TLS backend

Place this configuration in `config.yaml`. Connections for `tcp.example.com`
pass through to the TLS backend; LiteGate handles HTTPS for other hostnames:

```yaml
entrypoints:
  web:
    address: ":80"
  websecure:
    address: ":443"
    tls: true
    default: http
    on_non_tls: reject
    on_no_sni: reject
    inspect:
      timeout: 5s
      max_pending: 2048
      per_ip_pending: 16
    routes:
      - name: private-tls
        match:
          sni: tcp.example.com
        handle:
          proxy: tcp://127.0.0.1:444
```

`handle.proxy` does not terminate TLS. The backend must start a TLS handshake
from the first byte and hold the appropriate certificate. TCP Unix sockets such
as `unix:///run/service/tls.sock` are also supported.

#### Recommended: generate routes from Stream site shorthand

Simple configurations do not need explicit `routes`. Keep the global
`websecure` listener and define `streams/database.yaml`:

```yaml
site: tcp://db.example.com
name: database
proxy: 127.0.0.1:3306
```

This attaches to `websecure` and generates the SNI route automatically. Do not
repeat the hostname in `config.yaml`. TLS passes through by default. To terminate
TLS in LiteGate, configure Stream `tls.enabled: true` and a certificate source;
the backend specified by `proxy` then receives plain TCP.

For explicit routing to an existing Stream, merge the following route into
`entrypoints.websecure.routes`. The Stream named `database` must exist and use
`listen: false`. Choose exactly one of `handle.proxy` and `handle.stream` per route:

```yaml
entrypoints:
  websecure:
    address: ":443"
    tls: true
    routes:
      - name: database
        match:
          sni: db.example.com
        handle:
          stream: database
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `match.sni` | One hostname or a list; supports `*.example.com`. |
| `match.sni_regex` | SNI regular expressions; prefer `sni` for simple names. |
| `match.alpn` | Optional restriction to protocols offered in ClientHello, such as `[h2]`; case-sensitive. |
| `handle.proxy` | TCP / Unix socket backend receiving the original TLS bytes. |
| `handle.stream` | Existing named Stream applying its TLS, ACL and L4 proxy policies. |
| `default` | Unmatched routes fall back to HTTP/HTTPS processing; only `http` is supported. |
| `on_non_tls`, `on_no_sni` | Configure `http` or `reject` for non-TLS / missing SNI. |
| `inspect` | ClientHello inspection timeout and concurrency limits. |

Explicit routes for the same SNI without an ALPN restriction take precedence
over generated Stream routes. ALPN-scoped explicit routes claim only those
protocols; the generated route can still handle the rest. Plain TCP and UDP have
no TLS SNI and cannot use this mechanism for hostname routing. UDP/QUIC does not
use these TCP 443 routes. Avoid unintentionally assigning the same hostname to
an L4 Stream and an HTTP site: SNI dispatch happens before HTTP routing.
See the [L4 guide](l4-guide.md) for complete Stream scenarios.

## 2. Static TLS

```yaml
tls:
  enabled: false
  certs_dir: "./certs"

  # Local CA (self-signed and self-trusted, the equivalent of Caddy's tls internal)
  local_ca: false                       # issue leaf certificates for local domains on demand
  local_ca_domains: [".localhost", ".test"]   # allow-list of issuable domains (a leading dot means suffix match)
  local_ca_trust: false                 # install into the system trust store on first generation (local development only)
```

The local CA is the equivalent of Caddy's `tls internal`: it self-signs leaf certificates on demand for local domains. In `local_ca_domains`, a leading dot means suffix match. `local_ca_trust` installs the CA into the system trust store on first generation — enable it for local development only.

---

## 3. Auto-Cert

Setting `auto_cert.enabled: false` disables automatic issuance and renewal, including TLS handshakes and hot reloads. Enabled `dns_providers` groups are prepared before site certificates. Sites covered by a configured wildcard wait for that group; a failed group does not trigger a separate HTTP-01 order. Wildcards use DNS-01.

Auto-Cert is enabled by default; set `enabled: false` to disable issuance. Concrete domain sites using the standard HTTPS listener automatically prepare certificates after TCP 443 binds successfully. Existing valid exact, SAN, or wildcard certificates are reused first; missing certificates default to HTTP-01. HTTP-only `web` bindings, IP addresses, and wildcard routing patterns are excluded.

Site `https: true` controls HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects independently of issuance. HTTP-01 requires DNS pointing to this gateway and publicly reachable TCP 80. `on_demand.enabled` enables the additional SaaS authorization flow for domains not configured in advance; ordinary configured sites do not need it.

```yaml
auto_cert:
  enabled: true
  email: "litegate@example.com" # Default placeholder; replace if your CA requires a real address
  domains: []                    # legacy field, kept for compatibility
  certs_dir: "./certs"
  default_challenge: "http"      # default challenge type: "http" (port 80) or "tls-alpn" (port 443)
  storage_secret: ""             # Optional: symmetric key encrypting the ACME account private key (>= 32 bytes)

  # Multiple CA configuration
  ca_provider: "letsencrypt"     # letsencrypt, zerossl, google, custom
  acme_url: ""                   # custom ACME directory URL (required when ca_provider is custom)
  acme_ca_cert: ""               # private ACME root certificate path, or inline PEM
  acme_headers: {}                # extra headers for private ACME requests
  eab_kid: ""                    # External Account Binding key ID (ZeroSSL / GTS)
  eab_hmac: ""                   # External Account Binding HMAC key (ZeroSSL / GTS)

  provider: ""                   # legacy single-provider mode
  provider_config: {}

  dns_providers:
    - name: "aliyun-main"
      type: "aliyun"
      enabled: true
      domains: ["*.example.com", "example.com"]
      ddns:
        enabled: true
        ipv4: ""
        ipv6: ""
        sync_a: true
        sync_aaaa: true
        domains: ["*.example.com"]
      config:
        access_key_id: "..."
        access_key_secret: "..."

  renew_days: 10
  check_interval: 24
  use_staging: false
  propagation_dns: ["223.5.5.5", "114.114.114.114"]
  bootstrap_dns: ""

  dns_update:
    enabled: false
    auto_service_host_sync: false
    ip: ""
    key_prefix: "litedns/v1/records/"
    node_id: ""
    record_ttl: 30
    heartbeat_interval: 30s

  on_demand:
    enabled: false
    ask: "http://your-api/check-domain"
    kv_prefix: ""
    saas_template_site: ""

  webhook_url: ""
  webhook_token: ""
```

Field reference:

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `enabled` | bool | Enables automatic certificates; defaults to `true`; set `false` to disable issuance |
| `ca_provider` | string | Certificate authority provider. Defaults to `letsencrypt` |
| `acme_url` | string | Custom ACME directory URL. Required when `ca_provider=custom` |
| `eab_kid` | string | External Account Binding key ID (mandatory for ZeroSSL/GTS) |
| `eab_hmac` | string | External Account Binding HMAC key (mandatory for ZeroSSL/GTS) |
| `storage_secret` | string | Optional AES-256-GCM key encrypting the ACME account private key at rest. Must be at least 32 bytes |
| `dns_providers` | array | Multiple DNS provider configurations |
| `ddns.ipv4` / `ddns.ipv6` | string | Pin the IP manually |
| `dns_update` | object | Publishes this gateway's internal IP per domain into LiteMesh KV for LiteDNS internal resolution (requires litemesh) |
| `on_demand.ask` | string | Authorization check URL for on-demand issuance |
| `on_demand.kv_prefix` | string | KV prefix holding on-demand domain authorizations |
| `on_demand.saas_template_site` | string | Template site SaaS domains bind to |

### 3.1 Encrypted ClientHello (ECH)

Enable browser-to-gateway ECH in the main configuration using an existing enabled DNS provider:

```yaml
ech:
  enabled: true
  groups:
    - public_name: ech.example.com
      dns_provider: aliyun-main
    - public_name: ech.example.net
      dns_provider: cloudflare-main
  storage: file
  # For shared storage:
  # storage: kv
  # kv:
  #   provider: litemesh  # or consul, reuse the existing connection
  #   key_prefix: litegate/ech/mycluster/
  # key_prefix: litegate/ech/mycluster/
```

Disabled by default. Requires `auto_cert.enabled: true`, the `websecure` TCP listener on port 443, site TLS policies permitting TLS 1.3, and a built-in Aliyun or Cloudflare provider. Names must be concrete ASCII hostnames. Sites need direct A/AAAA records, without CNAME; Cloudflare records must be DNS only.

LiteGate arranges the public-name certificate, persists ECH keys, and publishes HTTPS DNS records with TTL 600. Keys rotate every 7 days; old keys stay accepted for 14 days after no potentially published records reference them. Failed writes retry every minute, and unmanaged HTTPS records are never overwritten. Configuration changes require a restart. Persist and back up `auto_cert.certs_dir/ech/<public_name>/state.json` (falling back to `tls.certs_dir`; matching legacy single-group state directories remain in use). Auto storage encrypts and shares state through Consul/LiteMesh only when config_watch is enabled; a publisher lease selects one DNS writer. Explicit storage: file supports one instance; storage: kv requires kv.provider (litemesh or consul) and kv.key_prefix. Root KV prefixes are parent directories; group prefixes are exact, and the state/publisher keys are appended. Explicit KV with local site files warns that every node must have identical sites. Withdraw HTTPS records and wait for DNS caches before disabling ECH. See [ECH](../06-certificates/ech.md) for deployment details.

## 4. Consul

```yaml
consul:
  enabled: false
  address: "127.0.0.1:8500"
  datacenter: "dc1"
  token: ""
  roles:
    config_watch: false
    cert_storage: false
    service_register: false
  keys:
    config_prefix: "litegate/config/sites/"
    cert_prefix: "litegate/certs/"
    stream_prefix: "litegate/streams/"
  service:
    id: ""
    name: "litegate"
    address: ""   # Registered address; auto-detects the outbound IP when empty
    tags: ["gateway", "edge"]
    meta:
      version: "1.0"
```

## 6. Service discovery

```yaml
service_discovery:
  catalogs:
    - enabled: false
      provider: "consul"          # consul / discovery
      name: ""                    # plugin discovery instance name, unique within a type
      config: {}                  # plugin-specific key/value configuration
      url: "127.0.0.1:8500"
      service_name: ""
      resolve_via: ""             # consul / litemesh
      default_domain: ""
      auth_mode: "disabled"       # disabled / auto
      token: ""
      namespace: ""
      jwt_auth_url: ""
      md5_auth_url: ""

    - enabled: false
      provider: "docker"
      socket_path: "/var/run/docker.sock"
      network_mode: "internal"     # internal (container network IP) or external (host port-mapped IP)
      swarm_mode: false            # enable Swarm mode (false enables adaptive detection)

  tag_entrypoints:
    allowed_ports: []              # ports service tags may open (HTTP entrypoints and TCP/UDP streams), e.g. [8080, 15432]
```

Service tags (`litegate.entrypoints.<name>.address`, `litegate.tcp.port`, `litegate.udp.port`) may open a listener only on a port listed in `tag_entrypoints.allowed_ports`, and never with the name or port of an entrypoint in this file. When the list is empty, tags cannot open ports and may only reference existing entrypoints (`web` and `websecure` by default). See the Service Tags Guide.

`network_mode` selects between the container network IP (`internal`) and the host port-mapped IP (`external`). `swarm_mode` left at `false` enables adaptive detection.

> [!NOTE]
> `catalogs` is an array. The old single-object `catalog` form is gone from the current code.
> An external discovery provider uses its registered name as `provider`, keeps its own settings under `config`, and can use `name` to distinguish several instances of the same type.

## 7. Cache and Redis

```yaml
cache:
  local_ttl: "60s"
  proxy_cache_max_entries: 10000  # maximum reverse-proxy cache entries; evicted by LRU to prevent OOM
  redis:
    enabled: false
    mode: "standalone"              # standalone or cluster
    address: "localhost:6379"
    addr: ""                      # alias for address
    addrs: []                     # Redis Cluster nodes, e.g. ["redis-1:6379", "redis-2:6379"]
    username: ""
    password: ""
    db: 1
    tls: false
    pool_size: 20
    min_idle_conns: 5  # legacy compatibility; Redigo creates connections on demand
    dial_timeout: "3s"
    read_timeout: "2s"
    write_timeout: "2s"
    max_retries: 2

redis:
  enabled: false
  mode: "standalone"
  address: "localhost:6379"
  addr: ""
  addrs: []
  username: ""
  password: ""
  db: 0
  tls: false
  pool_size: 20
  min_idle_conns: 5  # legacy compatibility; Redigo creates connections on demand
  dial_timeout: "3s"
  read_timeout: "2s"
  write_timeout: "2s"
  max_retries: 2
```

`proxy_cache_max_entries` bounds the reverse-proxy content cache, evicting by LRU so it cannot grow into an OOM. `addr` is an alias for `address`; `addrs` lists Redis Cluster nodes.

## 9. Dashboard / metrics / pprof

```yaml
dashboard:
  enabled: true
  port: 9999
  username: "admin"
  password: "$2a$..."
  token: ""                      # management API token, checked against the X-API-Key header
  cookie_secret: ""              # cookie encryption key (AES-256)
  allowed_origins: []            # origins allowed for CORS and WebSocket access (empty means same-origin only)
  require_secure_cookie: false   # require the dashboard session cookie to travel over HTTPS only

metrics:
  enabled: false
  port: 9090

pprof:
  enabled: false
  port: 6060
```

`token` is the management API token checked against the `X-API-Key` header. `allowed_origins` lists origins allowed for CORS and WebSocket access; empty means same-origin only.


### Go runtime (runtime)

Tunes the Go garbage collector (GC). When omitted, Go's defaults apply and behavior is unchanged.

```yaml
runtime:
  gc_percent: 200        # same as GOGC, 25-1000; omit for Go's default of 100
  memory_limit: 1GiB     # same as GOMEMLIMIT, units B/KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB, at least 64MiB
```

* **`gc_percent`**: how far, as a percentage of the live heap, the heap may grow before the next collection. LiteGate keeps little resident memory, so under the default it can collect dozens of times per second at high load; `200` noticeably reduces collections (about +13% throughput for a `respond` site on 16 vCPUs) at the cost of more memory.
* **`memory_limit`**: a soft memory cap; near it the collector runs earlier and more often. Set it whenever you raise `gc_percent` so memory cannot grow unbounded; keep it below the machine or container memory with headroom for other processes. Raising `gc_percent` without a limit logs a startup warning.
* An explicitly set `GOGC` / `GOMEMLIMIT` environment variable takes precedence; the matching field is ignored with a warning.
* Changing `runtime` requires a process restart; hot reload rejects the change.

## 10. Logging

```yaml
log:
  level: "info"                  # debug / info / warn / error
  format: "console"              # console / json

  webhook:
    enabled: false
    url: "https://example.com/webhook"
    levels: ["error", "fatal", "panic"]
    headers:
      Content-Type: "application/json"

  access_log:
    enabled: true
    stdout: true
    level: info
    file_enabled: false
    file: "" # defaults to ./logs/access.log when file_enabled is true
    max_size: 100         # Optional. Maximum size of one log file, in MB
    max_age: 7            # Optional. Maximum age of a rotated log file, in days
    max_backups: 30       # Optional. Maximum number of rotated log files kept
    compress: true        # Optional. Gzip rotated log files
    routing_detail: false
    webhook:
      enabled: false
      url: "http://mq-gateway:8080/access-log"
      batch_size: 100
      interval: "1s"
      headers:
        Authorization: "Bearer token"
```

`max_size` is per-file in MB, `max_age` the retention in days, `max_backups` the number of rotated files kept, and `compress` gzips them.

## 13. Auth providers

```yaml
auth_providers:
  google:
    enabled: true
    type: "oidc"
    issuer: "https://accounts.google.com"
    client_id: "..."
    client_secret: "..."
    scopes: ["openid", "email", "profile"]
    callback_path: "/_auth/callback/google"
    notify_url: ""
    clock_skew: "5m"
    allowed_signing_algs: ["RS256"]
    introspection_url: ""
    introspection_interval: "5m"

  github:
    enabled: true
    type: "oauth2"
    client_id: "..."
    client_secret: "..."
    scopes: ["read:user", "user:email"]
    auth_url: "https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize"
    token_url: "https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token"
    callback_path: "/_auth/callback/github"
```

Field reference:

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `type` | string | Authentication protocol type: `oidc` or `oauth2` |
| `issuer` | string | OIDC Discovery Issuer URL (required for OIDC, LiteGate fetches `.well-known/openid-configuration` automatically) |
| `client_id` | string | OAuth2 / OIDC Client ID |
| `client_secret` | string | OAuth2 / OIDC Client Secret |
| `scopes` | string[] | Requested OAuth2 scopes (default `["openid", "email", "profile"]`) |
| `callback_path` | string | OAuth2 callback path (default `/_auth/callback/<provider>`) |
| `notify_url` | string | Optional. Webhook URL to notify business systems on token events |
| `auth_url` | string | Authorization endpoint for standard non-OIDC OAuth2 providers |
| `token_url` | string | Token exchange endpoint for standard non-OIDC OAuth2 providers |
| `user_info_url` | string | Optional OAuth2 user-info JSON endpoint, called with a bearer token. GitHub defaults to its `/user` endpoint; errors reject login. Configure this for identity-based access rules with generic OAuth2. |
| `clock_skew` | string | Nonnegative OIDC tolerance for expiry, issued-at and not-before checks, e.g. `5m`; default `0` uses strict checks. |
| `allowed_signing_algs` | string[] | Allowed JWT signing algorithms, e.g. `["RS256", "ES256"]` |
| `introspection_url` | string | RFC 7662 Token Introspection endpoint |
| `introspection_interval` | string | Token introspection refresh interval, e.g. `5m` |
| `auth_params` | map | Adds or overrides authorization request parameters (e.g. `prompt: login`); an empty value removes a default. Google defaults to `access_type: offline` and `prompt: consent`; other IdPs get none |

---

## 14. OIDC security

```yaml
oidc_security:
  token_allowed_ips: []
  me_allowed_ips: []
  token_one_shot: false
  cookie_secret: ""
  cookie_same_site: "lax"        # lax / strict / none
  max_concurrent_sessions: 10
  token_endpoint_enabled: false  # enables /_litegate/oauth/token
  refresh_allowed_ips: []        # callers of /_litegate/oauth/refresh; loopback only by default
  allowed_redirect_hosts: []     # external hosts allowed as redirect_back targets
  login_failure_limit: 20        # failed login callbacks per IP within 15 minutes; negative disables
```

---

## 15. Real IP

```yaml
real_ip:
  # Trusted reverse proxy / load balancer IPs, whose X-Forwarded-For the gateway resolves the real client IP from
  trusted_proxies:
    - "127.0.0.1/32"
    - "10.0.0.5/32"
  # Internal client IPs/ranges allowed to perform east-west instance routing via X-Selector-Sid
  selector_trusted_clients:
    - "127.0.0.1/32"
    - "10.0.0.0/8"
```

* **`trusted_proxies`**: which upstream proxies the gateway trusts when resolving the real client IP from `X-Forwarded-For`. Normally just the specific IPs of your front-facing load balancers. Empty by default: no peer is trusted, `X-Forwarded-For` is ignored and the client IP is the direct connection address. When nginx or another proxy runs on the same host in front of LiteGate, add `127.0.0.1` explicitly.
* **`selector_trusted_clients`**: the networks allowed to perform east-west instance routing via `X-Selector-Sid`. Only requests originating inside these ranges may have that header honoured for physical instance isolation; a `X-Selector-Sid` arriving from anywhere else is stripped at ingress, so it cannot be forged externally. If unset, this falls back to `trusted_proxies`.

---

## 16. Other

```yaml
sites_dir: "./sites"
streams_dir: "./streams"
# disable_trace_id: true   # Omitted = automatic: in performance mode no trace IDs unless tracing or the access log is enabled; an explicit true/false wins

# Session-affinity cookie key (32-byte hex). Every node in a multi-node deployment
# must share the same value, or a sticky cookie cannot be decrypted across nodes. Pairs with lb_policy: cookie
sticky_key: ""

# OpenTelemetry distributed tracing (OTLP/HTTP)
tracing:
  enabled: false
  endpoint: "http://127.0.0.1:4318" # OTLP/HTTP receiver address (/v1/traces is appended)
  service_name: "litegate"
  sample_ratio: 1.0                  # sample ratio 0.0 - 1.0 (1.0 samples everything)
  trust_incoming_sampled: true       # trust the sampled flag on an incoming traceparent
  batch_size: 128
  interval: "2s"

# Passive health checking and outlier detection
passive_health:
  consecutive_failures: 5            # consecutive failures before the node is ejected
  base_ejection_time: "3s"           # first ejection duration
  max_ejection_time: "30s"           # maximum ejection duration under exponential backoff
  ejection_reset_time: "30s"         # how long a node must run cleanly before the duration decays back to the base

# External plugin directory, loaded dynamically
# plugin_config:
#   path: "./plugins"
#   watch: true
```

`sticky_key` is a 32-byte hex key for session-affinity cookies. Every node in a multi-node deployment must share the same value, otherwise a sticky cookie issued by one node cannot be decrypted by another. It pairs with an action's `lb_policy: cookie`.

Under `tracing`, `endpoint` is the OTLP/HTTP receiver (`/v1/traces` is appended automatically) and `sample_ratio` runs from 0.0 to 1.0.

Under `passive_health` (outlier detection), a node is ejected after `consecutive_failures`, held out for `base_ejection_time` growing exponentially up to `max_ejection_time`, and decays back to the base duration after `ejection_reset_time` of stable operation.

## 18. Scan protection

`scan_protection` blocks scanners dynamically using a threat score, banning the source IP when it probes sensitive paths (`.git`, `.env`) or non-existent APIs.

```yaml
scan_protection:
  enabled: false                      # master switch, off by default. Can be toggled at runtime from the dashboard or API
  block_duration: "1h"                # ban duration; h/m/s accepted
  max_404_attempts: 6                 # 404 probes tolerated per observation window; beyond it the score rises and blocking starts
  observation_period: "1m"            # length of the sliding observation window
  block_direct_ip: false              # leave false when rolling out; switch to true once no legitimate traffic is affected. Blocks requests reaching the gateway by raw IP with no Host
  forbidden_paths:
    - ".env"
    - ".php"
    - ".jsp"
    - ".asp"
    - ".aspx"
    - "/wp-admin"
    - "/wp-content"
    - "/phpmyadmin"

  global_rules:
    - name: "block_unsupported_ext"
      match:
        path_exact:
          - ".php"
          - ".php3"
          - ".php5"
          - ".php7"
          - ".phtml"
          - ".pht"
          - ".asp"
          - ".aspx"
          - ".ashx"
          - ".asmx"
          - ".jsp"
          - ".jspx"
          - ".cgi"
          - ".cfm"
      action: "deny"
      score: 30
      reason: "unsupported_ext_probe"

    - name: "secrets_and_vcs"
      match:
        path_exact:    ["/.git", "/.svn", "/.env", "/.htpasswd"]
        path_contains: ["/.git/", "/.env.", "/id_rsa", "/.ssh/", "/.aws/credentials", "/.docker/config.json"]
      action: "deny"
      score: 30
      reason: "secret_or_vcs_probe"

    - name: "admin_tool_probe"
      match:
        path_prefix:   ["/phpmyadmin", "/pma", "/adminer", "/manager/html", "/cgi-bin/"]
        path_contains: ["/vendor/phpunit/"]
      action: "deny"
      score: 30
      reason: "admin_tool_probe"
```

Leave `block_direct_ip` at `false` when first rolling this out, and turn it on once you have confirmed no legitimate traffic is affected; it immediately blocks requests that reach the gateway by raw IP with no Host header.

Field reference:

| Field | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `enabled` | bool | Enable scan protection. Can be toggled at runtime from the dashboard or API. |
| `block_duration` | string | How long a ban lasts, e.g. `"1h"` or `"30m"`. |
| `max_404_attempts` | int | Maximum 404 probes tolerated within the observation window. |
| `observation_period` | string | Length of the sliding observation window. |
| `forbidden_paths` | string[] | Sensitive path prefixes and suffixes. |
| `block_direct_ip` | bool | Block requests that address the gateway by IP directly. |
| `global_rules` | array | Blocking rules pairing a match with an action. Supported actions: `deny`, `tarpit`, `rate_limit`, `score`, `observe`. |

---

## 19. LiteGate Connect

Connect lets a Home node initiate a tunnel to Cloud and publish Home Sites through Cloud ports 80/443:

```yaml
connect:
  server:                         # Cloud node
    enabled: true
    hostname: connect.example.com
    path: /_litegate/connect/v1
    state_file: data/connect-registry.json
    health:
      enabled: false              # Optional: probe published domains end-to-end
      node_name: cloud-node-01    # Unique node name (optional, defaults to hostname)
      advertise_addr: 10.0.0.5    # Cloud address published to LiteDNS / LiteMesh
      advertise_port: 443
      probe_path: /healthz        # Probed through the Connect reverse tunnel
      probe_interval: 5s
      probe_timeout: 2s
      ttl: 15s                    # Used only when service_registration is enabled
      fail_threshold: 2
      max_concurrent_probes: 32
      dns_registration:           # Publish passing domains to LiteDNS KV; default off
        enabled: false
        key_prefix: litedns/v1/records/
        record_ttl: 10
        kv_ttl: 15s
      service_registration:       # Register passing domains as LiteMesh services; default off
        enabled: false
    peers:
      private:
        token_file: /etc/litegate/secrets/private-connect.token
        allowed_domains: ["*.private.example.com"]
        max_sites: 200
        max_connections: 4096
        sessions: 2
        max_registrations_per_minute: 30

  client:                         # Private node
    enabled: true
    name: private
    remote: https://connect.example.com/_litegate/connect/v1
    token_file: /etc/litegate/secrets/private-connect.token
    publish_sites: true
    publish_streams: false
    sessions: 2
    max_connections: 4096
    registration_debounce: 500ms
    exclude_domains: [connect.example.com]
```

Cloud and Private normally use separate configurations and enable only their respective side. See `docs/en/user/09-advanced/connect.md` for the complete field reference, security boundaries, mTLS, multiple Cloud nodes, token rotation, and rollout procedure.

Health probing does not publish anything unless one of the two registration switches is enabled. `dns_registration` writes one expiring LiteDNS KV record per passing domain and Cloud node; `service_registration` is optional for applications that still use the LiteMesh service-discovery SDK. The switches are independent and both default to `false`.


## Custom access log templates

```yaml
log:
  format: json
  access_log:
    enabled: true
    stdout: true
    file_enabled: true
    file: ./logs/access.log
    template: '{client_ip} - [{timestamp}] "{method} {uri}" {status} {size_bytes} "{referer}" "{user_agent}" {cost_ms}'
```

`template` formats access log stdout and files. Leave it empty to preserve existing output. Application logs still use `log.format`; webhooks and dashboard data remain structured. Rotation, asynchronous output and level filtering still apply.

Fields: `timestamp`, `client_ip`, `method`, `path`, `uri` (including the query), `host`, `status`, `size_bytes`, `cost_ms`, `upstream`, `route`, `site`, `trace_id`, `referer`, `user_agent`. Timestamps use the existing structured log timestamp; costs are milliseconds with fractional precision. Empty Referer and User-Agent values become `-`. Missing values become `-`. Newlines, control characters, quotes and backslashes in field values are escaped to prevent forged log lines. Templates must be single-line; unknown or malformed placeholders fail configuration validation. This uses LiteGate `{field}` syntax rather than Nginx `$variables`.

Restart LiteGate after changing `log.access_log.template`. Only `log.level` is hot-reloadable among global log settings. MCP saves validate the configuration and request a reload, but a successful save does not mean startup-only settings are active. `litegate -init` includes an empty template and a custom template example in its generated configuration.

### Shared matchers and configuration fragments

`matchers` and `snippets` are not main configuration. Definitions shared across sites live in `sites/_shared.yaml` (in KV mode, the `_shared.yaml` key under the sites prefix); see "Shared matchers and configuration fragments" in the site configuration reference. Writing these keys at the top level of `config.yaml` fails at load time.

## Upstream DNS resolvers

Changes to `resolvers` require a restart in Consul/LiteMesh `config_watch` mode. Filesystem reloads revalidate sites and reject removal of referenced resolvers. Stable ECH publication checks DNS every 30 minutes; failures retry every minute. To disable ECH, stop the instance, run `litegate ech withdraw -config config.yaml` to withdraw owned HTTPS records, then wait for caches to expire. Public-name certificate domains are derived at runtime without changing provider configuration.

```yaml
resolvers:
  corp:
    servers: [192.168.1.53:53, 192.168.1.54:53]
    timeout: 2s
```

Proxy objects and named Services reference this configuration with `resolver: corp`. Servers must be literal IP:port addresses (bracket IPv6); the default per-server query timeout is 2 seconds. Truncated UDP replies retry over TCP. Failed queries try backup servers in the same DNS view; NXDOMAIN / NODATA do not. Explicit resolvers bypass system DNS, hosts and environment HTTP proxies. Unconfigured upstreams retain existing behavior. New connections re-query DNS; existing connections can be reused. See [Upstream DNS](upstream-dns.md).

Set site-level `ech: ech.example.com` or `ech: ech.example.net` to select the public name and its DNS provider; domains are derived automatically. Boolean true is accepted only with one group; false disables ECH. Groups independently manage keys, rotation, DNS publication and KV leases. Default prefixes are litegate/ech/<public_name>/. Root key_prefix is a parent directory; group-level key_prefix is an exact, unique prefix. Legacy single-group configs keep their original state path and litegate/ech/default/ prefix. Site selection reloads live; group configuration changes require restart.

Third-party ECH DNS providers implement `plugin.HTTPSDNSProvider` and register the `https_records` capability. LiteGate owns ECH keys, rotation, KV synchronization, leases and retries; plugins only publish/withdraw public HTTPS records. HTTPS-only providers need separate certificate coverage; their domain selectors are excluded from certificate DNS-01 routing at runtime.
